title: Whitespace & Punctuation Normalization — lab sandbox
content:
Quick notes and experimental ruleset for whitespace & punctuation normalization decisions — personal sandbox.

Goal:
- Capture edge cases and an initial rulebook to decide when we transform raw input before labeling vs when we leave it verbatim. Focus: NER / span labels and short text relevance scoring where punctuation/spacing matters.

Principles (working):
1) Minimize labeler cognitive load: if a normalization step would change span boundaries in more than ~5% of examples, prefer marking ’normalize’ as an explicit preproc step and show examples.
2) Preserve human-intent tokens: punctuation used intentionally (em dashes to mark parentheticals, ellipses as pause, emoticons) should usually be kept.
3) Standardize accidental noise: repeated whitespace, stray control chars, zero-width spaces, and non-breaking spaces -> normalize to single ASCII space except where they join tokens intentionally.
4) Log transforms: every automatic transform needs a small provenance tag (e.g., __norm:ws-collapsed__) in the metadata so we can revert for audits.

Edge cases and suggested decisions (examples & rationale):
- Trailing/leading spaces: strip (unless label includes leading whitespace explicitly, extremely rare).
  Example: "  Acme Corp" -> "Acme Corp" (strip)

- Internal multiple spaces or tabs -> collapse to single space by default. Rationale: tokenization and downstream classifiers expect single whitespace.
  Example: "Acme   Corp" -> "Acme Corp"

- Non-breaking space (\u00A0): normalize to ASCII space.

- Hyphens vs. en-dash/em-dash: preserve characters but normalize sequences for matching. Don't collapse hyphenated tokens.
  Example: "state-of-the-art" keep as-is; "word -- aside -- word": consider mapping spaced double-hyphen to em-dash token but preserve spacing around it.

- Punctuation adjacent to entities: default: keep punctuation as part of token stream, but when computing entity spans for annotation we recommend labelers exclude leading/trailing punctuation unless punctuation is semantically part of the entity (e.g., company names ending with a punctuation mark is rare).
  Examples: 
    "Visit Acme, Inc. today" -> label span "Acme, Inc."? Prefer: label "Acme, Inc." and record rule used. But for strict NER matching we may also store canonical form "Acme Inc" in metadata.

- Parentheses/brackets: preserve and include in span only if part of the entity (notes often include bracketed nicknames). For automated canonicalization strip outer parens when producing normalized name.

- Possessives and contractions: keep apostrophes ("John's", "don't") as part of token; entity labeling should allow possessive suffix inside span if it belongs to entity mention.

- Ellipses and sequences of punctuation: preserve as-is; collapse >4 repeated punctuation to 3 for readability in UI (but keep an audit of original).
  Example: "Nooooo!!!!" -> store original, but for model input optionally compress ("Noo!").

- Emojis: keep. For entity spans, treat emoji as standalone tokens. Consider separate label class for emoji-suffixed mentions if it changes semantics.

- URLs, emails, mentions (@), hashtags (#): keep raw; provide optional normalization to canonical host or lowercased username when generating features.

- Quotation marks and smart quotes: normalize smart quotes to ASCII quotes only when downstream models need ASCII, but preserve original in audit log.

Short examples matrix (raw -> normalized -> label guidance):
- "Acme\u00A0Corp" -> "Acme Corp" -> label "Acme Corp" (span covers both tokens)
- "(Acme)" -> "(Acme)" (norm: parens kept), label: recommend excluding parens unless explicitly part of brand stylization
- "john.o'reilly@example.com" -> keep; do not split on dots for email-based NER
- "New\u2013York" (en-dash) -> keep; normalize for matching to "New-York" or "New York" variants in canonicalization outside labeling

Open questions / TODO (experiments):
- Evaluate impact of collapsing internal punctuation on recall for brand name detection (A/B small sample). Jira: JIRA-4287 assigned.
- Empirically measure how often labelers include trailing punctuation in span; if >15% variance, add explicit UI toggle.
- Run tokenization mismatch audit: compare spaCy/byte-level tokenizers vs our canonical tokenizer on a 2k sample and measure span-offset drift.
- Prototype metadata flags in ingestion pipeline (__norm:ws-collapsed__, __norm:smartquotes-ascii__, __norm:emoji-preserve__) and add to annotation DB.

Quick regexes to try (notes to self):
- collapse whitespace: s/\u00A0|\s+/ /g (but keep \n as sentence boundary in some tasks)
- strip control chars: s/[\x00-\x1F\x7F]+//g
- repeated punctuation collapse: s/(\p{Punct})\1{3,}/$1$1$1/g

Labeler UI guidance (short):
- Always work on the preview that shows ORIGINAL text and NORMALIZED preview side-by-side.
- When in doubt, highlight the minimal human-meaningful token span. Mark "norm-ignore" checkbox if you intentionally include punctuation as part of the entity.
- Add a short note when you deviate from the default rule (free-text "why").

Notes to self / scratches: 
- Lucas mentioned wanting a separate normalization pipeline vs in-editor transforms — lean toward pipeline + preview so labelers see canonicalization but can choose verbatim.
- Keep sample set for audit (200 ex) covering currencies, hyphenates, emojis, non-breaking spaces, smart quotes, emails, URLs.

References and past findings:
- Prior label audit (2023-11) found heavy variance on punctuation inclusion for organization labels (F1 drop if we auto-strip commas).
- Thread: #labeling-heuristics on Slack (search "punctuations") has follow-ups — pull examples into sample set.

Next steps (short):
- Build 200-sample test harness (Maya) by 2025-02-01.
- Add tokenization mismatch check (Jamal) and push minimal transform flags to ingestion.
- Draft small one-pager for labeling team with 10 canonical examples and UI screenshots (goal: reduce labeler variance).

Unresolved: how to treat languages with meaningful non-space token boundaries (Chinese/Japanese) — defer to localization leads and include in sample set.

End of sandbox notes. Will iterate when experiments come back.
